stage_a.note: Meagan smiles constantly and delivers her pitch with very strong enthusiastic engagement.
She is highly animated, smiling, and clearly excited about her product and business.
Her delivery is very friendly, approachable, and she smiles warmly at the panel.

venture.description: Artificial floral bouquets and arrangements made from recycled and sustainable materials like wood, paper, and burlap.
venture.note: Direct to consumer online sales, recently expanding into the wedding industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan introduces Eco Flower, explaining the problem with real flowers and presenting her sustainable, recycled alternative.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan begins handing out customized bouquets and gifts to the panel.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Robert receives a customized map made of flowers showing Croatia and Australia.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara receives a spring-themed bouquet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan hands Kevin a bouquet and explains the matching boutonniere.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin smells the flowers and notes that they are scented.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan hands out gifts to Daymond and Mark.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond examines his lapel flower.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan explains that Mark's bouquet is made with real money.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin comments on the money bouquet and jokes about spending it.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Robert asks Meagan if she individually makes all of the flowers herself.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan explains she used to make them but now uses two manufacturers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark notes that needing manufacturers is a positive sign.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Robert asks the female investors how they would feel receiving fake flowers instead of real ones.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan begins to react to Robert's question before Lori interjects.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori states that giving fake flowers shows a lack of sensitivity and she prefers real ones.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan counters that her customers cherish the flowers forever because they do not die.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark suggests Meagan share her sales figures to prove the other investors wrong.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan agrees to share her sales numbers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for her total sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan reveals lifetime sales of 2.8 million dollars over a year and a half, entirely direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks for the retail price of her bridal bouquet bundle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan states the bridal bouquet sells for fifty-nine dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks Meagan how she came to start the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan explains she was inspired by watching Shark Tank and developed the idea with her father.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori points out that similar products exist and asks about competition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan clarifies that while crafters exist, nobody else offers a ready-to-buy online bouquet for gifting.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin argues that fake flowers are not heavily used in the wedding industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan explains she recently entered the wedding market and achieved significant sales in a single day.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what drove the sudden spike in daily sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan explains she ran a four thousand dollar ad campaign after previously holding back on marketing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what her typical daily sales were prior to the ad campaign.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan states typical daily sales were between six and thirteen thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark calculates the return on ad spend and praises her success.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how much of her own money she invested in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan says she invested seven hundred dollars and shares her difficult living situation before finding an investor.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Robert asks how much equity she sold to her first investor and for what amount.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan explains she gave up twenty-five percent for three thousand dollars in inventory and rent coverage.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks if she has taken on any additional investors since then.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan says she later sold fifty percent to a local investment firm for thirty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin calculates that Meagan is left with only twenty-five percent ownership.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Robert confirms that she sold seventy-five percent of her company for roughly thirty-five thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan confirms the equity split and attributes it to desperate times.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin exits, stating he refuses to invest for ten percent and taking more would leave her as an employee.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that diluting her further would wipe out her ownership and make her an employee.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan explains that any new equity would come equally from all partners, and she wants to buy out her investors.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if her current investors would be willing to be bought out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan believes Mark's contacts could help facilitate a buyout or restructure the equity.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Robert exits, advising her to retain equity and stating he does not want to partner with her current investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara exits, explaining that she does not understand the appeal of artificial flowers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark exits, praising her success but stating the business is outside his area of expertise.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori exits, feeling there is too much competition and the product is not unique enough for her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin repeats that investing without wiping out her remaining equity is virtually impossible.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan defends her position, emphasizing that she is doing a great job running the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond offers four hundred thousand dollars for twenty-five percent of the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan expresses concern that giving up twenty-five percent would wipe out her remaining equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond clarifies that the twenty-five percent would dilute all partners equally, not just her.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan counters Daymond's offer, asking if he would accept twenty percent instead.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond insists on twenty-five percent, explaining it makes him an equal fifth partner.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan accepts Daymond's offer of four hundred thousand dollars for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond confirms the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Meagan hugs Daymond and thanks the panel for the opportunity.

decisions.note: Refuses to invest for 10% and believes taking 30% would wipe her out.
Thinks she should retain as much equity as possible and doesn't want to partner with her current investors.
She doesn't understand the appeal of fake flowers and wouldn't buy them.
Thinks she is doing amazing but it is not his area of expertise.
Believes there is too much competition and the product is readily available elsewhere.
Offers to become an equal fifth partner.
Asks to lower the equity to 20% to avoid too much dilution.
Accepts Daymond's explanation of 5% dilution per partner.
